scenario: AITA for telling my SIL to shut up? | My SIL drives me a little bonkers sometimes. She is extremely proud of things like not watching TV, not listening to pop music, not having Facebook, and she interrupts conversations to say it. Often insulting the thing as well, instead of just saying that she doesn’t like it. Instead it’s about her superiority for not liking it. A few days ago we were having dinner and my 14-year-old sister starts talking about she watched a Marvel movie and she’s looking forward to a sequel that should be coming out soon. My SIL said, “I’ve never watched any Marvel movies. They seem pretty awful.” I was pissed off, I don’t get why my SIL, an adult woman, feels the need to be so rude and dismissive towards a teenager. I said loudly, “shut up, not everything has to be about you and what you like.” She blushed and didn’t say anything more, my brother didn’t say anything either. But he messaged me after they left saying that this was my expression of “always hating” his wife and that I’m a bad person who doesn’t want her to participate in conversation. AITA?

By setting aside a specific day to confront and acknowledge past mistakes, individuals can develop a greater sense of accountability and responsibility for their actions. This intentional reflection can lead to a deeper understanding of the consequences of their mistakes and a stronger motivation to make amends and change their behavior. Having a dedicated day for introspection can also help individuals develop a greater sense of self-awareness, which can, in turn, influence their decision-making and behavior throughout the year. By regularly examining their actions and their impact on others, individuals may become more mindful of the potential consequences of their choices and more inclined to consider the well-being of those around them. Moreover, the annual practice of Yom Kippur can foster a sense of humility and recognition of one's own fallibility. This can lead to a greater willingness to apologize, make amends, and learn from mistakes, rather than trying to justify or deny them. By acknowledging and accepting their mistakes, individuals can develop a more growth-oriented mindset, which can help them approach challenges and setbacks with a greater sense of resilience and determination. It's also worth noting that the act of seeking forgiveness and making amends can have a profound impact on relationships and personal growth. By taking responsibility for past wrongs and working to repair harm, individuals can strengthen their connections with others, rebuild trust, and develop a greater sense of empathy and compassion. Overall, having a day like Yom Kippur can indeed change how seriously one takes their mistakes and can have a lasting impact on personal growth, relationships, and overall well-being.
